_about: Public-domain Hugh of Saint Victor (about 1096-1141, canon regular of Paris) in English for the Word Hoard: the Explanation of the Rule of St Augustine, tr. Aloysius Smith (London: Sands, 1911), from an Internet Archive scan. Richard of Saint Victor has no pre-1930 English beyond the anonymous Middle English Benjamin in Gardner's anthology, so he has no shelf. Added 2026-10-17 by lane A, round 26 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Translators recorded per item where the title page names one; every printing dated or catalogued before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted. Taylor's Didascalicon (Columbia, 1961) added 2026-11-03 by the non-renewal sweep: a US book never renewed, US public domain.

hugh-explanation-rule: Explanation of the Rule of St Augustine, tr. Aloysius Smith (London: Sands, 1911)

_alternates.hugh-rule-bruges: The Rule of the Great S. Augustin expounded by Hugh of S. Victor, from the French of Charles de la Grange (Bruges: John de Cock; catalogued 1735): English translator not named

_excluded.hugh-late: Post-1929 translations still in copyright or with no open scan: Soliloquy 1956 (Kevin Herbert, Franciscan Institute: not checked), De sacramentis 1951 (see _pending). Taylor's Didascalicon (1961) moved onto the shelf 2026-11-03: never renewed.

_rights_checked.hugh-didascalicon-taylor: Non-renewal sweep 2026-11-03 (Adam: "I want everything that was not renewed"). Jerome Taylor (American, University of Notre Dame); first published New York, Columbia University Press, 1961, so a US work (URAA does not reach it). Renewal search: pipeline/renewal_check.py over NYPL's cce-renewals (every renewal 1950-1991; this one was due in 1989), surname 'taylor' with 'didascalicon': no renewal. The scan's own record agrees: University of Florida, 'Copyright status reviewed by UF staff - Out of copyright'. US public domain by non-renewal.
